			<font style="display: inline;">We are a holding company with no operations of our own. Accordingly, our working capital needs and our ability to service debt and pay dividends on our common and preferred stock is dependent on the distribution of cash from our subsidiaries. Each of our subsidiaries is a distinct legal entity, and, under certain circumstances, legal, contractual and debt covenant restrictions contained in existing financing agreements may limit or prevent any of them from making distributions to us. In addition, future financing or other arrangements entered into by our subsidiaries could limit their ability to make distributions to us. In the event that we do not receive adequate distributions from our subsidiaries, we may not be able to meet our working capital needs and may be unable to service our debt or make dividend payments on our common or preferred stock. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Cancellation of or modifications to the Immigrant Investor Program, or our failure to successfully raise capital under the program's guidelines, could adversely affect our ability to execute our growth strategy and improve our resorts.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">We have funded certain capital projects, and may fund other future capital projects, by raising funds under the Immigrant Investor Program (the &#x201C;EB-5 Program&#x201D;), administered by the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (the &#x201C;USCIS&#x201D;) pursuant to the Immigration and Nationality Act. This program was created to stimulate the U.S. economy through the creation of jobs and capital investments in U.S. companies by foreign investors. </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">Under the EB-5 Program, an annual allocation of immigrant visas (&#x2018;&#x2018;EB-5 Visas&#x2019;&#x2019;) is made available for qualified individuals seeking lawful permanent resident status on the basis of their investment in a new commercial enterprise that generates jobs. Recently, the demand for the annual allocation of EB-5 Visas has exceeded the supply, and potential investors may be subject to lengthy waiting periods for such visas. These waiting periods could exceed five to ten years. Furthermore, raising funds pursuant to the EB-5 Program could become significantly more difficult if the primary EB-5 investor markets in Asia are impacted by economic downturn or military conflict, or if the USCIS subjects EB-5 investor applicants to lengthy adjudications.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The EB-5 Program </font><font style="display: inline;">is</font><font style="display: inline;"> not a permanent program and has been extended on a year-to-year basis. The continuity of the EB-5 Program is dependent on future action by Congress and is subject to political uncertainty, and Congress may materially modify aspects of the EB-5 Program in ways that would make it unfeasible for us to rely on EB-5 financing for future financing. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We cannot guarantee we will be able to rely on the EB-5 Program as a potential source of funding to implement future plans to improve our resorts. In this case, conventional financing options, such as loans, may prove too costly or may not be available, which could result in cancellation of our development and improvement plans and could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">We rely on one primary lender and its affiliates as the source for the majority of our financing and credit. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We have historically relied on one lender and its affiliates, </font><font style="display: inline;">EPR Properties </font><font style="display: inline;">(&#x201C;EPR&#x201D;), for substantially all of our financing and credit needs, including financing relating to our resort acquisitions. As of April 30, 2018, amounts due to EPR totaled </font><font style="display: inline;">$1</font><font style="display: inline;">14</font><font style="display: inline;">.2 million.</font><font style="display: inline;"> EPR is an entertainment, entertainment-related, recreation and specialty real estate company with its common stock listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "EPR". In the event EPR is not available to extend us credit, we may not be able to obtain financing on terms as favorable to us as those under our arrangements with EPR. As a result, we may be subject to more stringent financial covenants and higher interest rates. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">EPR has an option to purchase, or assume our leases relating to, certain of our ski resorts. If EPR exercises this option, we would incur significant tax obligations. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Pursuant to the terms of our borrowing agreements with EPR, we have entered into an option agreement (the &#x201C;Option Agreement&#x201D;) that provides EPR with a purchase option on our Boston Mills, Brandywine, Jack Frost, Big Boulder and Alpine Valley ski resorts. The purchase option is exercisable as to any one or more of such properties on the maturity date of the applicable underlying promissory note at a purchase price to be calculated in accordance with the terms of the Option Agreement. Upon the closing of any sale under the Option Agreement, EPR will enter into an agreement with the Company or one of its subsidiaries for the lease of each such acquired property for an initial term of 20 years, plus options to extend the lease for two additional periods of 10 years each.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We have a low adjusted tax basis in these properties as we have taken tax depreciation since the time they were acquired. As a result, we would realize significant taxable gains on the sale of the properties if EPR exercises a purchase option, and we may be required to pay substantial income taxes on taxable gains from any such sale. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Under certain circumstances, our insurance coverage may not cover</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"> all possible losses, and we may not be able to renew our insurance policies on favorable terms, or at all. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Although we maintain various property and casualty insurance policies, our insurance policies do not cover all types of losses and liabilities, and our levels of coverage may not be sufficient to cover the ultimate cost of claims. If we are held liable for amounts exceeding the limits of our insurance coverage or for claims outside the scope of our coverage, it </font><font style="display: inline;">could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

Our ability to obtain future insurance coverage at commercially reasonable rates could be adversely affected if we or other companies within or outside our industry sustain significant losses or make significant insurance claims. </font>

			<a name="_Hlk518896568"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">We qualify as an emerging growth company and a non-accelerated filer under Rule 12b-2 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. As a result, we are not required by Section&nbsp;404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act to have our independent registered public accounting firm attest to the effectiveness of our internal controls over financial reporting and are able to use extended transition periods for complying with new or revised accounting standards. </font>

		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">Our management is required by Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act to make a formal assessment of the effectiveness of our internal controls over financial reporting. Our independent registered public accounting firm, however, is not required to attest to the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting until such time as we are no longer either i) an emerging growth company or ii) a non-accelerated filer as defined by Rule 12b-2 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. This lack of attestation by our independent registered accounting firm may increase the risk that we fail to detect and remedy any weakness of deficiencies in our internal control over financial reporting. Additionally, at such time as we are subject to the auditor attestation requirements, our independent registered public accounting firm may issue a report that is adverse in the event it is not satisfied with the level at which our controls are documented, designed or operating. If we are unable to establish and maintain effective internal controls it </font><font style="display: inline;">could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>

As a result, our financial statements and disclosures may not be comparable to other companies who do not qualify as an emerging growth company. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">The issuance of shares of our Series A Preferred Stock reduces the relative voting power of holders of our common stock, may dilute the ownership of such holders and may adversely affect the market price of our common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">As holders of our Series A Preferred Stock are entitled to vote, on an as-converted basis, together with holders of our common stock on all matters submitted to a vote of the holders of our common stock, the issuance of the Series A Preferred Stock effectively reduces the relative voting power of the holders of our common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;Current stockholders have no preemptive rights to purchase any </font><font style="display: inline;">securities</font><font style="display: inline;"> in order to maintain their proportionate interest in the Company.&nbsp; </font>

Sales by holders of a substantial number of shares of our common stock in the public market, or the perception that such sales might occur, could have a material adverse effect on the price of our common stock.&nbsp; </font>

			<font style="display: inline;">The Investor and it</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> affiliates currently own </font><font style="display: inline;">approximately 10.0% of the outstanding shares of our common stock. Assuming the conversion of the </font><a name="_Hlk517795244"></a><font style="display: inline;">Series A Preferred Stock</font><font style="display: inline;"> and exercise of the Warrants also owned by the Investor, the Investor would own 36.7% of the outstanding shares of our common</font><font style="display: inline;"> stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additional pre-emptive rights and rights of first offer in the documents governing the Private Placement of our Series A Preferred Stock may allow the Investor to maintain its ownership position.&nbsp;&nbsp;Holders of our Series A Preferred Stock are entitled to vote, on an as-converted basis, together with holders of our common stock on all matters submitted to a vote of the holders of our common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, the holders of shares of the Series A Preferred Stock have the ability to significantly influence the outcome of any matter submitted for the vote of the holders of our common stock. </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">Under the terms of the Series A Preferred Stock, the Series A Preferred Stock generally ranks, with respect to the liquidation, dividends and redemption, senior to other securities.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Stockholders&#x2019; Agreement provides that, so long as the Investor beneficially owns, on an as-converted basis, at least 11.4% of the outstanding&nbsp;&nbsp;equity securities of the Company,&nbsp;&nbsp;the Investor&#x2019;s approval is required in order for the Company or any subsidiary to i) materially change the nature of its business from owning, operating and managing ski resorts or ii) acquire or dispose of any resorts, assets or properties for aggregate consideration equal to or greater than 30% of the enterprise value of the Company and its subsidiaries.&nbsp; </font>

Any transaction which may be so discouraged or avoided could be a transaction that the Company's common stockholders might consider to be in their best interests. Furthermore, as the sole holder of our Series A Preferred Stock, the Investor is entitled to vote, on an as-converted basis, together with holders of our common stock on all matters submitted to a vote of the common stockholders. On an as-converted basis</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and assuming the exercise of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">the W</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">arrants</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, the Investor would own approximately 36.7% of the common stock. As</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> a result, the Management Stockholders together with the Investor will be able to exercise a significant level of control over all matters requiring stockholder approval, including the election of directors, amendment to our amended and restated articles of incorporation and approval of significant corporate transactions. This ability could have the effect of delaying or preventing a change of control of the Company or changes in management, and will make the approval of certain transactions difficult or impossible without the support of these stockholders. It is possible that these persons will exercise control over us in a manner adverse to your interests. </font>

		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">In fiscal 2015, the Company&#x2019;s board of directors approved the commencement of a regular quarterly cash dividend on our common stock at a quarterly rate of $0.1375 per share.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">In April 2016, the board suspended common stock dividends in consideration of our then current operating performance, debt agreement covenant compliance and liquidity position. We resume</font><font style="display: inline;">d quarterly dividend payments in February 2017.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;The board approved the reinstatement of the dividend in February 2017 at the quarterly rate of $0.07 per share and declared dividends during the </font><font style="display: inline;">fiscal year ended April 30, 2017 and April 30, 2018 </font><font style="display: inline;">as noted in the table above.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">We cannot assure you that this dividend rate will be sustained or that we will continue to pay dividends in the future. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The declaration and payment of future dividends to holders of our common stock will be at the sole discretion of our board of directors, subject to applicable state law, and will depend on many factors, including our actual results of operations, financial condition, capital requirements, contractual restrictions, restrictions in our debt agreements, economic conditions and other factors that could differ materially from our current expectations. As a holding company, our ability to declare and pay dividends is also dependent on our subsidiaries&#x2019; ability to make cash available to us by dividend, distribution or otherwise.</font><font style="display: inline;"> Each of our subsidiaries is a distinct legal entity, and, under certain circumstances, legal and contractual restrictions may limit our ability to obtain cash from them.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Provisions included in the agreements governing certain of our debt prohibit and/or limit the Company and its subsidiary borrowers from paying dividends or otherwise making distributions under certain circumstances. For example, we are prohibited from paying dividends if the fixed charge coverage ratio, as defined by the applicable agreements, is below 1.25:1.00 and during default situations. For a more complete description of the dividend restrictions included in our debt agreements, see Item 7, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#x2014;Liquidity and Capital Resources&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;">Financing Arrangements</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D; and Note 4, &#x201C;Long-term Debt</font><font style="display: inline;"> and Revolving </font><font style="display: inline;">Credit</font><font style="display: inline;"> Facilities</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D; to our consolidated financial statements.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of April 30, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">8</font><font style="display: inline;">, the Company is in compliance with all debt covenants.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:1.2pt 28.8pt 0pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On November 2, 2016, the Company issued $20 million of Series A Preferred Stock to the Investor in the Private </font><font style="display: inline;">Placement. </font><font style="display: inline;">C</font><font style="display: inline;">umulative dividends accrue on the outstanding shares of Series A Preferred Stock on a daily basis in arrears at the rate of 8% per annum on the liquidation value of $1,000 per share.&nbsp;All accrued and accumulated dividends on the Series A Preferred Stock shall be paid prior and in preference to any dividend or distribution on any junior securities, including the Company&#x2019;s common stock, provided that the Company may declare or pay any dividend or distribution payable on the common stock in shares of common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The Certificate of Designation of the Series A Preferred Stock provides that,</font><font style="display: inline;"> until the earlier of (i) such date as no Series A Preferred Stock remains outstanding and (ii) January 1, 2027, the Company is prohibited from paying any dividend on capital stock when there are accrued or unpaid dividends with respect to the Series A Preferred Stock. </font><font style="display: inline;">For a more complete description of the dividend restrictions included in the Certificate of </font><font style="display: inline;">Designation relating to the Series A Preferred Stock, see </font><font style="display: inline;">Item 7, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#x2014;Liquidity and Capital Resources&#x2014;</font><font style="display: inline;">Liquidity and </font><font style="display: inline;">Significant </font><font style="display: inline;">Uses</font><font style="display: inline;"> of Cash&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;"> and Note 5, &#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">Series A Preferred Stock</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D; to our consolidated financial statements.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 9pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-size:9.5pt;">Item 7.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Management&#x2019;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10.8pt 0pt 0pt;line-height:10.75pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;vertical-align:baseline;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The following discussion of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and the notes thereto included elsewhere in this </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Report.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">Overview</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">We own or lease and operate 14 ski resorts throughout the Midwestern, Northeastern and Southeastern (which includes Pennsylvania) United States. Our ski resorts, which include both day ski resorts and overnight drive ski resorts, offer snow skiing, snowboarding and other snow sports. During the last two ski seasons, we had an </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">average </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">1.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">6</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> skier</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> visits each year.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">We operate in a single </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">reportable </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">business segment&#x2014;resort operations. The consolidated financial data presented in this</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> &nbsp;R</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">eport is comprised of the data of our 1</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">4</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> ski resorts. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The opening and closing dates of our ski resorts are dependent upon weather conditions, but our peak ski season generally runs from early December </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">through</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> mid-April. See Item 1, &#x201C;Business&#x2014;Seasonality&#x201D; for </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">information about the historical </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">opening and closing dates for our resorts.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">L</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ike other day ski resort and overnight drive ski resort operators, </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">we </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">earn our revenues in six principal categories. In order of their contribution, they are: lift</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and tubing</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> tickets, food and beverage sales, equipment rentals, hotel/lodging, ski instruction, and retail. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 1pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:1pt;background-color:yellow;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Our largest source of revenue is the sale of lift tickets (including season passes) which represented </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">approximately 46.8</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">%</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, 47.1% and 47.6% of net revenue for the years ending April 30, 2018, 2017 and 2016, respectively. Lift ticket revenue is driven by the volume of lift tickets and season passes sold and the pricing of these items. Most of our season pass products are sold before the start of the ski season. For the 20</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">1</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">7/2018, 2016/2017 and 2015/2016 ski seasons, approximately 36.3%,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">34.5%</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> and 38.1</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">%, respectively, of total lift revenue recognized was comprised of season pass revenue.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Season pass revenue, although collected prior to the ski season, is recognized </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ratably </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">over the ski season based upon the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">number of days our resorts are open</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The cost structure of our operations has significant fixed and variable components. Our significant variable expenses include retail and food and beverage cost of sales, labor costs and power and utilities. As such, operating margins can fluctuate based on the level of revenues.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">Recent Developments</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">2017 Tax Act</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">On December 22, 2017, the United States government enacted comprehensive tax legislation commonly referred to as the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (the &#x201C;2017 Tax Act&#x201D;). The 2017 Tax Act made broad changes to the federal tax code which impacts us. The 2017 Tax Act included provisions that, among other things, provide for i) the reduction of the federal corporate tax rate, ii) the elimination of the corporate alternative minimum tax, iii) a new limitation on the deductibility of interest expense, iv) changes in the treatment of net operating losses after December 31, 2017, and v) bonus depreciation that allows for full expensing of qualified property.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">Subsequent to the passage the 2017 Tax Act, </font><font style="display: inline;">SEC</font><font style="display: inline;"> issued Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 118 (&#x201C;SAB 118&#x201D;), which provides guidance on accounting for the impact of the 2017 Tax Act. SAB 118 provides for a measurement period, not to exceed one year from enactment of the 2017 Tax Act, for companies to complete accounting for the impact of the 2017 Tax Act under the </font><font style="display: inline;">FASB&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;"> Accounting Standards Codification 740, &#x201C;Income Taxes&#x201D; (&#x201C;ASC 740&#x201D;). In accordance with SAB 118, a company must reflect the income tax effect of those aspects of the 2017 Tax Act for which the accounting under ASC 740 is complete. To the extent that a company&#x2019;s accounting for income effects of the 2017 Tax Act is incomplete, but the company can determine a reasonable estimate, the company must record a provisional estimate in its financial statement. If a company cannot determine a provisional estimate, it should continue to apply ASC 740 on the basis of the provision of the tax laws that were in effect immediately before the enactment of the 2017 Tax Act. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We recorded an income tax benefit of $4.0 million for the year ended April 30, 2018, which includes a $0.1 million discrete benefit at the 2017 Tax Act enactment date and an additional benefit of $3.5 million which was directly attributable to the impact of the 2017 Tax Act&#x2019;s reduced corporate tax rate that became effective January 1, 2018. The additional benefit arises because we are a calendar year taxpayer and the seasonality of our business results in significant losses during the first eight months of fiscal</font><font style="display: inline;"> 2018</font><font style="display: inline;"> which produce a federal benefit at </font><font style="display: inline;">the prior corporate tax rate of </font><font style="display: inline;">34%</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> and significant income during the period January to April 2018 which </font><font style="display: inline;">was</font><font style="display: inline;"> subject to the lower 21% corporate tax rate </font><font style="display: inline;">implemented by</font><font style="display: inline;"> the 2017 Tax Act . </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">Our effective tax rate for the period from the enactment of the 2017 Tax Act through the end of our fiscal year ending April 30, 2018, was </font><font style="display: inline;">27.0</font><font style="display: inline;">%. </font>

Mr. Mueller stepped down from his position as the Company&#x2019;s Chief Financial Officer and Secretary on October 3, 2017 and assumed a new role as Executive Vice President.&nbsp;&nbsp;In connection with this transition, Christopher J. Bub became our Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Secretary. Mr. Bub previously served as the Company&#x2019;s Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Tahoma;">&#xFEFF;</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Royal Banks of Missouri Credit Facilities</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On October 27, 2017, we renewed and increased our existing credit facility with Royal Banks of Missouri (the &#x201C;2017 Royal Banks Credit Facility&#x201D;). The 2017 Royal Banks Credit Facility provides for a $10 million working capital line of credit to be used for general business purposes and a $15 million acquisition line of credit to be used i) to pay off $12.4 million of principal and accrued interest outstanding under the previous credit agreement with Royal Banks of Missouri (the &#x201C;Original Credit Facility&#x201D;) and ii) for the acquisition of additional ski resort properties. On October 27, 2017, we used $12.4 million of the borrowing capacity available under the acquisition line of credit to pay off all outstanding amounts under the Original Credit Facility, including amounts outstanding under a term loan which bore interest at the prime rate plus 1.00% per annum with an original maturity date of January 26, 2020. As of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">April 30, 2018</font><font style="display: inline;">, approximately $12.4 million was outstanding under the </font><font style="display: inline;">acquisition line of credit and no amounts were outstanding under the working capital line of credit. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The term of the 2017 Royal Banks Credit Facility is 14 months with loans payable in monthly interest only installments charged at the bank&#x2019;s prime rate plus 1.00% per annum, with any outstanding principal amounts due at the end of the term. Beginning on January 31, 2018, we </font><font style="display: inline;">were</font><font style="display: inline;"> required to fund a debt service account by depositing in three equal monthly installments an amount equal to the estimated annual interest due in connection with outstanding loans under the 2017 Royal Banks Credit Facility. We are required to maintain a minimum debt service coverage ratio (as defined in the credit agreement) of 1.25 to 1.00. In addition, were our fixed charge coverage ratio (as defined in the credit agreement) to fall below 1.50 to 1.00, we would be required to prefund certain other debt service payments, and should the ratio fall below 1.25 to 1.00, we would be prohibited from paying </font><font style="display: inline;">common or preferred </font><font style="display: inline;">dividends. The 2017 Royal Banks Credit Facility is secured by the assets of our subsidiaries which operate our Hidden Valley, Paoli Peaks, Snow Creek, Crotched Mountain and Attitash resorts. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;">During the year ended </font><font style="display: inline;">April 30</font><font style="display: inline;">, 2018, we incurred approximately $1.</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;"> million of fixed asset impairment losses in connection with our decision to cease operation of a restaurant and certain hotel-like amenities at a condominium building adjacent to our Attitash ski resort. In connection with our 2007 acquisition of the Attitash ski resort, we acquired property and equipment constituting the commercial core of a condominium building located adjacent to the resort. Since this acquisition, we have i) provided management services to the condominium&#x2019;s owners association under a management services agreement (the &#x201C;Management Services Agreement&#x201D;), ii) sponsored a rental management program whereby unoccupied condominium units </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">The Company conducts an assessment of the carrying value of goodwill annually, as of last day of March, or more frequently if circumstances arise which would indicate the fair value of a reporting unit with goodwill is below its carrying amount. As a result of the annual assessment as of March 31, 2018, the Company </font><font style="display: inline;">incurred an impairment loss of</font><font style="display: inline;"> $0.4 million of goodwill associated with the acquisition of its Alpine Valley ski resort. The Company did not record any impairment of goodwill for the years ended April 30, 2017 or 2016.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;">Seasonality</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our revenues are highly seasonal in nature. The vast majority of revenue is generated during the ski season, which occurs during the winter months in our third and fourth fiscal quarters.&nbsp;&nbsp;Some of our properties offer off season attractions, such as golf, roller coasters, swimming, summer concerts and zip rides; however, these activities do not comprise a substantial portion of our annual revenues.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;"> As a result, our resorts typically experience operating losses and negative operating cash flows during the first and second quarters of each fiscal year.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The seasonality of our revenues amplifies the effect of events outside our control, especially weather. While our geographically diverse operating locations help mitigate the effect of weather conditions, adverse weather could lower attendance due to suboptimal skiing conditions or limited access to our resorts, render snowmaking wholly or partially ineffective in maintaining ski conditions, and increase operating costs related to snowmaking efforts and inefficient labor utilization.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">During years ended April 30, 2018, 2017 and 2016, the percentage of revenue we recognized in our third and fourth fiscal quarters, combined, was </font><font style="display: inline;">87.6</font><font style="display: inline;">%,</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">87.3</font><font style="display: inline;">%</font><font style="display: inline;"> and</font><font style="display: inline;"> 87.9%,</font><font style="display: inline;"> respectively. As a result, the operating results for any quarterly period are not necessarily indicative of the results that may be achieved for any subsequent quarter or for a full year.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Weather Impact</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The timing and duration of favorable weather conditions </font><font style="display: inline;">significantly influences </font><font style="display: inline;">the timing and </font><font style="display: inline;">volume</font><font style="display: inline;"> of skier visits</font><font style="display: inline;"> and the associated revenue</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">While natural</font><font style="display: inline;"> snowfall early in the ski season </font><font style="display: inline;">influences </font><font style="display: inline;">skier visits, all of our ski resorts have snowmaking capabilities in the event that the natural snowfall is insufficient. Cold weather, however, is essential to a successful ski season</font><font style="display: inline;"> and t</font><font style="display: inline;">here is no way to predict </font><font style="display: inline;">future </font><font style="display: inline;">weather conditions. We sell season passes prior to the start of the ski season to help mitigate any negative effects unfavorable weather may have on our revenues.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During the 2017/2018 ski season we encountered significant weather-driven challenges, including bitterly cold weather which depressed skier visits at times and rainy weather during a holiday weekend which depressed skier visits during one of our historically busiest weekends. Favorable weather conditions in the Northeast towards the end of the ski season helped to mitigate the impact of unfavorable weather conditions in the middle of the season. Similarly, w</font><font style="display: inline;">e faced </font><font style="display: inline;">significant </font><font style="display: inline;">weather challenges during the </font><font style="display: inline;">2016/2017</font><font style="display: inline;"> ski season due to unseasonably warm weather in the Midwest</font><font style="display: inline;"> midway through the ski season.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In addition to our continued investment in snow making technologies and infrastructure, we rely on our season pass products to help mitigate the impact on our revenues from adverse weather.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Season Pass Products</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">For the 2016/2017 ski season we introduced the Peak Pass which allows skiers to utilize any of our resorts in the Northeastern or Southeastern (which includes Pennsylvania) United States. The introduction of the Peak Pass contributed to </font><font style="display: inline;">the </font><font style="display: inline;">increased revenue</font><font style="display: inline;"> we experienced</font><font style="display: inline;"> in our 2018 and 2017 fiscal years as compared to our 2016 fiscal year</font><font style="display: inline;">, despite significant weather challenges during those fiscal years.</font><font style="display: inline;"> Our pre-season season pass sales for the upcoming 2018/2019 increased </font><font style="display: inline;">16.0%</font><font style="display: inline;"> in </font><font style="display: inline;">dollar</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> and 14.0% in units as compared to the 2017/2018 season, and the 2017/2018 season pre-season pass sales increased 8.6% in both </font><font style="display: inline;">dollars</font><font style="display: inline;"> and units as compared to the same </font><font style="display: inline;">period </font><font style="display: inline;">for the 2016/2017 ski season. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Skier Visits</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Our ski resorts operate in the Northeast, Midwest and Southeast (which includes Pennsylvania) markets as defined by the Kottke Report. </font><font style="display: inline;">Our skier visits of 1.</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in fiscal 2018 </font><font style="display: inline;">were up </font><font style="display: inline;">7.4</font><font style="display: inline;">%</font><font style="display: inline;"> from fiscal 2017. This compares to a </font><font style="display: inline;">4.5</font><font style="display: inline;">% increase in total skier visits </font><font style="display: inline;">across the entire industry </font><font style="display: inline;">to Northeast</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> Midwest </font><font style="display: inline;">and Southeast </font><font style="display: inline;">resorts as reported by the Kottke Report. Our total resort visits, which include tub</font><font style="display: inline;">ing</font><font style="display: inline;"> visits, were up 7.1</font><font style="display: inline;">%</font><font style="display: inline;"> from fiscal 2017. Total visits to our Northeast </font><font style="display: inline;">and Southeast </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8pt;line-height:107.92%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 11pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Reported EBITDA</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Reported EBITDA is not a measure of financial performance under U.S. GAAP. </font><font style="display: inline;">We have chosen to include &#x201C;Reported EBITDA&#x201D; (which we define as net income before interest, income taxes, depreciation, amortization, gain on sale/leaseback, other income and expense and other non-recurring items) as a measurement of our results of operations because we consider this measurement to be a significant indication of our financial performance and available capital resources.&nbsp;&nbsp;Because of large depreciation and other charges relating to our ski resorts operations, it is difficult for management to fully and accurately evaluate our financial results and available capital resources using net income alone. In addition, the use of this non-U.S. GAAP measure provides an indication of our ability to service debt, and we consider it an appropriate measure to use because of our highly leveraged position.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We believe that by providing investors with Reported EBITDA, they will have a clearer understanding of our financial performance and cash flows because Reported EBITDA i) is widely used in the ski industry to measure a company&#x2019;s operating performance without regard to items excluded from the calculation of such measure; ii) helps investors to more meaningfully evaluate and compare the results of our operations from period to period by removing the effect of our capital structure and asset base from our operating results; and iii) is used by our board of directors, management and our lenders for various purposes, including as a measure of our operating performance and as a basis for planning.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The items we exclude from net income to arrive at Reported EBITDA are significant components for understanding and assessing our financial performance and liquidity. Reported EBITDA should not be considered in isolation or as an alternative to, or substitute for, net income, net change in cash and cash equivalents or other financial statement data presented in our consolidated financial statements as indicators of financial performance or liquidity. Because Reported EBITDA is not a measurement determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP and is susceptible to varying calculations, Reported EBITDA, as presented, may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures of other companies, limiting its usefulness as a comparative measure.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Reconciliations of net </font><font style="display: inline;">income (</font><font style="display: inline;">loss</font><font style="display: inline;">)</font><font style="display: inline;"> to Reported EBITDA</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">for the years ended April 30, 2018, 2017 and 2016, were as follows (dollars in thousands):</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8pt;line-height:107.92%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 11pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Year Ended </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">April 30, 2018</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">, Compared with the Year Ended April 30</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">, 2017</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Net Revenue.</font><font style="display: inline;"> Net revenue increased $8.</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;million, or 6.</font><font style="display: inline;">8</font><font style="display: inline;">%, for the year ended </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">April 30, 2018</font><font style="display: inline;">, compared with the year ended </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">April 30, 2017</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase is primarily attributable to increased resort attendance driven, in part, by earlier ski season opening dates which led to higher ticket, rentals, retail and food and beverage sales. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Resort Operating Costs.</font><font style="display: inline;"> Resort operating costs increased $9.</font><font style="display: inline;">3</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, or</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">10.</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">%, for the year ended </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">April 30, 2018</font><font style="display: inline;">, compared with the previous year.&nbsp;&nbsp;Labor costs increased by $4.8 million, or </font><font style="display: inline;">9.9</font><font style="display: inline;">%, due to i) lower pre</font><font style="display: inline;">-</font><font style="display: inline;">season staffing levels in fiscal 2017 as compared to fiscal 2018</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> ii) increased staffing needs </font><font style="display: inline;">due to</font><font style="display: inline;"> earlier ski season opening dates and higher attendance in fiscal 2018, and iii) increases in the minimum wage which impacted certain of our resorts. Other resort operating expenses increased by $3.0 million, or 14.6%, primarily as a result of increased maintenance and supplies costs. During fiscal 2017, we experienced low liquidity levels and, as a result, implemented employee furloughs and strict spending controls on discretionary costs.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">By the end of fiscal 2017, our liquidity levels had normalized. As a result, our staffing levels returned to a more normal level, and our resorts incurred increased costs as they prepared for the 2017/2018 ski season. </font><font style="display: inline;">Cost of goods sold related to food and beverage and retail sales increased $1.0 million, or 9.6%, due to increased food and beverage and retail sales</font><font style="display: inline;"> stemming from higher resort attendance.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Depreciation and Amortization</font><font style="display: inline;">. Depreciation and amortization increased by $0.5 million, or 4.1%, on a higher depreciable base which included, among other new assets, the West Lake Water project which was placed in service during the year.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">General and Administrative Costs</font><font style="display: inline;">. General and administrative expenses increased $0.4 million, or 6.7%, for the year ended </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">April 30, 2018 </font><font style="display: inline;">compared with the year ended </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">April 30, 2017</font><font style="display: inline;">, primarily due to </font><font style="display: inline;">higher</font><font style="display: inline;"> incentive compensation expense and lower professional fee expense.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Restructuring and Impairment. </font><font style="display: inline;">During the year ended April 30, 2018 we incurred restructuring and impairment charges totaling $2.1 million which included i) $1.7 million related to our decision to terminate a rental management program and cease operation of hotel-type amenities at a condominium property adjacent to our Attitash ski resort, and ii) </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.4 million related to </font><font style="display: inline;">the impairment of goodwill associated with our Alpine Valley ski resort. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Interest. </font><font style="display: inline;">Excluding amounts capitalized, interest expense increased by $0.8 million, or 6.8%, primarily as a result of increases in the interest rates on adjustable rate debt, partially offset by the effect of a $1.7 million net repayment of interest bearing debt over the course of the year.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Income Taxes.</font><font style="display: inline;"> The income tax benefit for the year ended April 30, 2018, </font><font style="display: inline;">was $4.0 </font><font style="display: inline;">million</font><font style="display: inline;">, which compares with income tax expense of $0.7 million for </font><font style="display: inline;">the year ended </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">April 30, 2017</font><font style="display: inline;">. The benefit for fiscal 2018 is </font><font style="display: inline;">primarily as result of positive impacts from the enactment of the 2017 Tax Act which, among other effects, i) reduced our deferred tax liabilities and ii) reduced our effective income tax rate for the four months ending April 30, 2018.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Year Ended </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">April 30, 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">7</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">, Compared with the Year Ended April 30</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">6</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:11pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The increase in skier and tube visits we experienced during fiscal 2017 as compared to fiscal 2016 was the primary driver for increases in six of our seven principal revenue categories.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company experienced improved weather conditions, specifically in the Northeast, which helped to drive additional skier visits. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times;">Lift and tubing revenue increased $12.6&nbsp;million, or 27.6%, for fiscal 2017 compared to fiscal 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;Season pass sales and seasonal program sales increased $2.7&nbsp;million, or 15.7%, from fiscal 2016 to fiscal 2017. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times;">Food and beverage revenue increased $7.3&nbsp;million, or 45.9%, for fiscal 2017 compared to fiscal 2016, $2.2 million of which was&nbsp;&nbsp;due to an increase in yield per skier and $5.1 million of which was </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times;">due to </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times;">increased skier visits.</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times;">An increase in rental revenue of $1.5&nbsp;million, or 22.0%, for fiscal 2017 compared to fiscal 2016 was offset by a decrease in yield per skier visit of $0.7 million. Ski instruction revenue increased $2.0&nbsp;million, or 30.1%, for fiscal 2017 compared to fiscal 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times;">Hotel and lodging revenue increased $1.8&nbsp;million, or 22.1%, for fiscal 2017 compared to fiscal 2016. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times;">Retail revenue increased $1.6&nbsp;million, or 35.9%, for fiscal 2017 compared to fiscal 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;">36</font><font style="display: inline;"></font>

		</p>

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times;">Revenue from summer activities increased $0.4 million, or 10.4%, for fiscal 2017 compared to fiscal 2016, which is primarily attributable to the inclusion of Hunter Mountain&#x2019;s results in the consolidated financial statements for all of fiscal 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;We acquired Hunter Mountain on January 6, 2016, and as such, its summer activities were not included in fiscal 2016 results.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times;">Other income increased $0.3 million, or 8.4%, for fiscal 2017 compared to fiscal 2016, as a result of the inclusion of Hunter Mountain&#x2019;s results in the consolidated financial statements for all of fiscal 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;Hunter Mountain&#x2019;s results were included only as of the acquisition date in fiscal year 2016. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The inclusion of Hunter Mountain&#x2019;s results in the consolidated financial statements for all of fiscal 2017 also contributed to increases in our expenses, as illustrated below.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Labor and labor related expenses increased $8.9 million, or 22.7%, for fiscal 2017 versus fiscal 2016</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times;">, $5.8 million of which was due to a longer operating season in fiscal 2017 compared to fiscal 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Retail and food and beverage cost of sales increased $3.1 million, or 39.9%, for fiscal 2017 versus fiscal 2016, </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times;">$1.4 million of which is</font><font style="display: inline;"> a result of increased retail and food and beverage revenue.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Power and utility expense increased $1.0 million, or 14.7%, for fiscal 2017 versus fiscal 2016. Of the increase, </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times;">$0.6 million is a result of increased snowmaking hours.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times;">Other operating expense</font><font style="display: inline;"> increased $2.1 million, or 11.4%, for fiscal 2017 versus fiscal 2016, $1.1 million of which is a result of the Hunter Mountain acquisition and the remaining </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times;">$1.0 million of which is a result of costs tied to increased resort visits, such as credit card processing fees, insurance, supplies, payroll processing fees, repairs and maintenance. </font><font style="display: inline;">Depreciation and amortization increased $2.0 million, or 18.7%, for fiscal 2017 versus fiscal 2016, as a result of the inclusion of Hunter Mountain&#x2019;s results in the consolidated financial statements for all of fiscal 2017.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">General and administrative expenses increased $0.9 million, or 20.3%, for fiscal 2017 versus fiscal 2016 primarily due to an increase in professional fees of $0.6 million related to incremental public company expenses and the Private Placement transaction and an increase in salaries and related benefits of $0.3 million. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Real estate and other taxes increased $0.4 million, or 20.2%, for fiscal 2017 versus fiscal 2016. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The increase in interest expense, net of $1.7 million was a result of the debt incurred in connection with the Hunter Mountain acquisition in the third quarter of fiscal 2016 and the debt incurred pursuant to the </font><font style="display: inline;">b</font><font style="display: inline;">ridge </font><font style="display: inline;">l</font><font style="display: inline;">oan </font><font style="display: inline;">a</font><font style="display: inline;">greement </font><font style="display: inline;">with EPR </font><font style="display: inline;">in fiscal 2017, </font><font style="display: inline;">which has been repaid</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Income tax increased $2.8 million as a result of an increase in the earnings before income tax expense of $7.3&nbsp;million for fiscal 2017 versus fiscal 2016.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Cash Flow</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Net cash </font><font style="display: inline;">used in o</font><font style="display: inline;">perating activities </font><font style="display: inline;">was $0.</font><font style="display: inline;">2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;"> for the year ended April 30, 2018, as compared with net cash provided by operating activities of</font><font style="display: inline;"> $12.7 million and $10.2 million for the years ended April 30, 2017 and 2016, respectively. The reduction in net cash provided by operating activities in fiscal 2018 as compared with fiscal 2017, is primarily due to the prepayment of interest to EPR</font><font style="display: inline;"> and lower income before income taxes</font><font style="display: inline;">. Under the terms of the various borrowing agreements we have with EPR, we are required to, at EPR&#x2019;s discretion, either prepay a certain amount of interest payments to EPR or deposit the equivalent amount of cash in a restricted account to fund interest payments to EPR. As of April 30, 2018, we had prepaid interest to EPR of $8.9 million</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> which is included in the caption prepaid </font><font style="display: inline;">expenses</font><font style="display: inline;"> and deposits in our consolidated balance sheet as of April 30, 2018. As of April 30, 2017, we had no prepaid interest to EPR, although we had deposited a similar amount of interest payments into a restricted cash account to fund interest payments to EPR, which was included in the caption restricted cash in our consolidated balance sheet for the year ended April 30, 2017. The increase in net cash provided by operating activities in fiscal 2017 as compared with fiscal 2016 was primarily the result of higher net income, </font>
		</p>

Cash used by investing activities during fiscal 2018 related to capital expenditures with the most significant expenditures related to the completion of the West Lake Water Project and ongoing construction of the Carinthia Base Lodge Project at Mount Snow. Cash used by investing activities in fiscal 2017 related entirely to capital expenditures. Cash used by investing activities in fiscal 2016 primarily included $33.4 million for the acquisition of the Hunter Mountain ski resort and $13.8 million for capital expenditures. The presentation of cash used by investing activities for the years ended April 30, 2017 and 2016, reflect</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> a change in the presentation of changes in restricted cash balances due to the adoption of a new accounting standard regarding the presentation of restricted cash in the statement of cash flows.</font>

During fiscal 2018 we made net repayments of borrowings of $5.9 million and made distributions to our common and preferred shareholders of $</font><font style="display: inline;">4.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million. Net cash flows provided by financing activities during fiscal 2017 primarily related to the $19.6 million of net proceeds from the issuance of our Series A Preferred Stock, partially offset by the payment of deferred financing costs of $4.5 million, the net repayments of borrowings of $3.4 million and distributions to our common shareholders of $1.0 million. Net cash flows provided by financing activities during fiscal 2016 primarily related to i) net proceeds of $35.1 million from borrowings to finance our acquisition of the Hunter Mountain ski resort and ii) the release of $22.0 million of EB-5 investor funds from escrow to fund construction of the West Lake Water project, partially offset by iii) the net repayment of other borrowings of $0.8 million, iv) distributions to our common shareholders of $7.7 million and v) the payment of deferred financing costs of $1.4 million. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;">Our available cash is consistently highest in our fourth quarter primarily due to the seasonality of our resort business. We had $23.1 million of cash and cash equivalents as of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">April 30, 2018</font><font style="display: inline;">, compared with $33.7 million at April 30, 2017. </font><font style="display: inline;">In addition, we had restricted cash balances on hand as of April 30, 2018, for i) the financing of our Carinthia Ski Lodge project and ii) interest payments on our revolving credit facilities in the amount of $12.2 million and $1.2 million, respectively. </font><font style="display: inline;">We generate the majority of our cash from operations during the ski season, which occurs during our third and fourth fiscal quarters. We currently anticipate cash flow from operations will continue to provide a significant source of our future cash flows</font><font style="display: inline;">, and </font><font style="display: inline;">believe that cash flow from operations, availability on credit facilities and available cash on hand will be sufficient to fund our recurring capital expenditure requirements and other currently anticipated cash needs for the next 12 months</font>

We also expect to spend approximately $6.0 million to $8.0 million on resort maintenance capital expenditures, which is consistent with our historical maintenance capital expenditures that are needed to maintain and improve the level of service and overall experiences we strive to provide our visitors. </font><font style="display: inline;">The Carinthia Ski Lodge Project is being funded with proceeds raised pursuant to the EB-5 Program.&nbsp;&nbsp;We currently plan to use cash on hand and/or cash flow generated from future operations to provide the cash necessary to execute our other capital projects and believe that these sources of cash will be adequate to meet our needs.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">Capital expenditures for fiscal 2017 were approximately $8.6 million, which reflects temporary decreased spending due to lower than normal liquidity levels </font><font style="display: inline;">experienced during fiscal 2017 </font><font style="display: inline;">as a result of unfavorably warm weather during the 2015/2016 ski season and unexpected delays in the release of EB-5 Program funds used to finance the West Lake Water project that was recently completed.</font>

We expect that we would finance the acquisition of any new ski resorts through a combination of cash on hand, existing credit facilities, new financing arrangements or the issuance of debt or equity.</font>

In addition, until the earlier of i) such date as no Series A Preferred Stock remains outstanding and ii) January 1, 2027, w</font><font style="display: inline;">e</font><font style="display: inline;"> are prohibited from paying any dividend on capital stock when there are accrued or unpaid dividends with respect to the Series A Preferred Stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;We intend to pay the Series A Preferred Stock dividends which are $1.6 million annually, or $0.4 million quarterly.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">EPR Secured Notes</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company has various secured borrowings (the &#x201C;EPR Secured Notes&#x201D;) under a master credit and security agreement and other related agreements, as amended, (together, the &#x201C;EPR Agreement&#x201D;) with EPR Properties and its affiliates (&#x201C;EPR&#x201D;). </font><font style="display: inline;">Each of the EPR Secured Notes is secured by one or more of the Company&#x2019;s resort properties and is guaranteed by the Company. </font><font style="display: inline;">The EPR Secured Notes bear interest at specified interest rates which are subject to increase each year by the lesser of i) three times the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (as defined) or ii) a capped index (the &#x201C;Capped CPI Index&#x201D;) which is 1.75% for the Hunter Mountain Secured Note and 1.50% for all other notes.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Financial covenants set forth in the EPR Agreement consist of i) a maximum leverage ratio (as defined) of 65%, above which the Company and certain of its subsidiaries are prohibited from incurring additional indebtedness, ii) a consolidated fixed charge coverage ratio (as defined) of 1.50:1.00 on a rolling four quarter basis, and iii) a prohibition of the Company paying dividends if the Company is in default (as defined) or if the fixed charge coverage ratio (as defined) is below 1.25:1.00. During the first two quarters of fiscal year 2017, the Company&#x2019;s fixed charge coverage ratio fell below 1.25:1.00 and, as a result, the Company was prohibited from paying dividends. As of April 30, 2018, the Company </font><font style="display: inline;">was</font><font style="display: inline;"> in compliance with all debt covenants.&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Non-financial covenants set forth in the EPR Agreement include i) restrictions on certain transactions, including mergers, acquisitions, leases, asset sales, loans to third parties, and the incurrence of certain additional debt and liens and ii) a requirement that the Company obtain the consent of EPR prior to redeeming any preferred or common stock.</font>
