		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In January 2017, the FASB issued ASU 2017-04, &#x201C;Intangibles-Goodwill and Other (Topic 350),&#x201D; which simplifies the existing guidance for testing goodwill for impairment. &nbsp;The new standard eliminates the current two-step approach used to test goodwill for impairment and requires an entity to apply a one-step quantitative test and record the amount of goodwill impairment as the excess of a reporting unit's carrying amount over its fair value, not to exceed the total amount of goodwill. The Company adopted this ASU on a prospective basis as of March 31, 2018, the date of its annual goodwill impairment test for its fiscal year 2018.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Recently Issued Accounting Standards</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company qualifies as an &#x201C;emerging growth company&#x201D; under the Jumpstart Our Business Startups Act of 2012, which provides that an emerging growth company may take advantage of an extended transition period for complying with new or revised accounting standards. As an emerging growth company, the Company may delay the adoption of certain accounting standards until those standards would otherwise apply to private companies. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<a name="_Hlk490649938"></a><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In February 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-02, &#x201C;Leases (Topic 842),&#x201D; which requires lessees to recognize most leases on the balance sheet. This ASU requires modified retrospective adoption and will be applicable for the Company as of April 30, 2020, with early adoption permitted. &nbsp;The Company is currently evaluating the impact the adoption of this ASU will have on its consolidated financial statements. While the Company expects the pattern of expense for leases it currently classified as operating will be similar between the old and new guidance, it expects adoption of the new standard will result in a significant increase in assets and liabilities for right of use assets and lease obligations, respectively, for leases it currently classifies as operating. As of April 30, 2018, future minimum lease payments under operating leases was approximately </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$14,712</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In May 2014, the FASB issued ASU 2014-09, &#x201C;Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606),&#x201D; which was subsequently modified by other ASUs from 2015 through 2017. This ASU, as amended, provides new guidance for the recognition of revenue and provides for a five-step analysis of transactions to determine when and how revenue is recognized. This ASU establishes a core principle that revenue is recognized to depict the transfer of&nbsp;goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration to which the entity expects to be entitled in exchange for those goods or services.&nbsp;&nbsp;It also requires additional disclosures regarding the nature, amount, timing and uncertainty of revenue and cash flows arising from contracts with customers.&nbsp; This ASU may be adopted using either a full or modified retrospective approach and will be applicable for the Company as of April 30, 2020, with early adoption permitted.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company expects to adopt this ASU using the full retrospective approach and does not expect the adoption of this ASU will have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:39.6pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In March 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-09, &#x201C;Compensation-Stock Compensation (Topic 718): Improvements to Employee Share-Based Payment Accounting,&#x201D; which provides new guidance related to accounting for share-based payments. </font>
		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">F - </font><font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;">13</font><font style="display: inline;"></font>

		</p>

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">This ASU requires entities to record the income tax effect of share-based payments when the awards vest or are settled, and clarifies the cash flow statement presentation of excess tax benefits and withholding tax payments. In addition, the ASU allows for a policy election to account for forfeitures either upon occurrence or by estimating forfeitures. This ASU requires prospective adoption and will be applicable for the Company as of April 30, 2019, with early adoption permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact the adoption of this ASU will have on its consolidated financial statements. </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Tahoma;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>

As a result of the annual assessment as of March 31, 2018, the Company recorded an impairment loss of $443 of goodwill associated with its Alpine Valley ski resort. The Company used a discounted cash flow approach with Level 2 and Level 3 inputs. As of April 30, 2018, the balance of goodwill relates entirely to the Company&#x2019;s Hunter Mountain ski resort.</font><font style="display: inline;"> The Company did not record any impairment of goodwill for the years ended April 30, 2017 or 2016.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">The Company has various secured borrowings (the &#x201C;EPR Secured Notes&#x201D;) under a master credit and security agreement and other related agreements, as amended, (together, the &#x201C;EPR Agreement&#x201D;) with EPR Properties and its affiliates (&#x201C;EPR&#x201D;). </font><font style="display: inline;">Each of the EPR Secured Notes is secured by one or more of the Company&#x2019;s resort properties and is guaranteed by the Company. The EPR Secured Notes bear interest at specified interest rates which are subject to increase each year by the lesser of i) three times the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (as defined) or ii) a capped index (the &#x201C;Capped CPI Index&#x201D;) which is </font><font style="display: inline;">1.75%</font><font style="display: inline;"> for the Hunter Mountain Secured Note and </font><font style="display: inline;">1.50%</font><font style="display: inline;"> for all other notes.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The Company has determined the Capped CPI Index features represent an embedded derivative; however, this derivative does not require bifurcation and separate presentation at fair value because the Capped CPI Index feature is closely related to the debt instrument.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">Financial covenants set forth in the EPR Agreement consist of i) a maximum leverage ratio (as defined) of </font><font style="display: inline;">65%</font><font style="display: inline;">, above which the Company and certain of its subsidiaries are prohibited from incurring additional indebtedness, ii) a consolidated fixed charge coverage ratio (as defined) of </font><font style="display: inline;">1.50</font><font style="display: inline;">:1.00 on a rolling four quarter basis, and iii) a prohibition of the Company paying dividends if the Company is in default (as defined) or if the fixed charge coverage ratio (as defined) is below </font><font style="display: inline;">1.25</font><font style="display: inline;">:1.00. During the first two quarters of fiscal year 2017, the Company&#x2019;s fixed charge coverage ratio fell below 1.25:1.00 and, as a result, the Company was prohibited from paying dividends. As of April 30, 2018, the Company was in compliance with all debt covenants.&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">Non-financial covenants set forth in the EPR Agreement include i) restrictions on certain transactions, including mergers, acquisitions, leases, asset sales, loans to third parties, and the incurrence of certain additional debt and liens and ii) a requirement that the Company obtain the consent of EPR prior to redeeming any preferred or common stock. </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">The EPR Agreement also provides that none of the EPR Secured Notes may be prepaid without the consent of EPR and that any default under any of the EPR Secured Notes, lease agreements between the Company and EPR, or credit facilities with other lenders would constitute a default under all EPR Secured Notes and lease agreements. A change in control (as defined) would also constitute an event of default.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">An additional contingent interest payment would be due to EPR if, on a calendar year basis, the gross receipts (as defined) from the properties securing the EPR Secured Notes (the &#x201C;Gross Receipts&#x201D;) are more than the result (the &#x201C;Interest Quotient&#x201D;) of divid</font><font style="display: inline;">i</font><font style="display: inline;">ng the total interest charges for the EPR Secured Notes by a certain percentage rate (the &#x201C;Additional Interest Rate&#x201D;). In such a case, the additional interest payment would equal the difference between the Gross Receipts and the Interest Quotient multiplied by the Additional Interest Rate. This calculation is made on an aggregated basis for the notes secured by the Company&#x2019;s Jack Frost, Big Boulder, Boston Mills, Brandywine, Alpine Valley and Hunter Mountain ski resorts, where the Additional Interest Rate is </font><font style="display: inline;">10%</font><font style="display: inline;">, and is made on a standalone basis for the note secured by the Company&#x2019;s Mount Snow ski resort, where the Additional Interest Rate is </font><font style="display: inline;">12%</font><font style="display: inline;">. The Company has not made any additional interest payments on the EPR Secured Notes based on these provisions.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The EPR Agreement grants EPR certain other rights including i) an option to purchase the Company&#x2019;s </font><font style="display: inline;">Boston Mills, Brandywine, Jack Frost, Big Boulder and Alpine Valley resorts exercisable on the maturity dates of the applicable promissory notes for such properties,, ii) a right of first refusal through 2021, subject to certain conditions, to provide all or a portion of the financing associated with any purchase, ground lease, sale/leaseback, management or financing transaction contemplated by the Company with respect to any new or existing ski resort properties, and iii) a right of first refusal through 2021 to purchase the Company&#x2019;s Attitash ski resort in the event the Company were to desire to sell the Attitash ski resort</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> To date, EPR has not exercised any purchase options. If EPR exercises a purchase option, EPR will enter into an agreement with the Company for the lease of each acquired property for an initial term of </font><font style="display: inline;">20</font><font style="display: inline;"> years, plus options to extend the lease for </font><font style="display: inline;">two</font><font style="display: inline;"> additional periods of </font><font style="display: inline;">ten</font><font style="display: inline;"> years each.</font>

As of April 30, 2018, the Company had prepaid interest to EPR of </font><font style="display: inline;">$8,905</font><font style="display: inline;"> which is included in the caption prepaid expenses and deposits. As of April 30, 2017, the Company had no prepaid interest to EPR, although it had </font><font style="display: inline;">$8,775</font><font style="display: inline;"> of restricted cash to fund interest payments to EPR.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;;font-size: 12pt"><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">The Company serves as the general partner for two limited partnerships,</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">Carinthia Group 1, LP and Carinthia Group 2, LP (together, the &#x201C;Limited Partnerships&#x201D;), which were formed to raise </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">$52,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> through the Immigrant Investor Program administered by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (&#x201C;USCIS&#x201D;) pursuant to the Immigration and Nationality Act (the &#x201C;EB-5 Program&#x201D;). The EB-5 Program was created to stimulate the U.S. economy through the creation of jobs and capital investments in U.S. companies by foreign investors. The program allocates immigrant visas to qualified individuals (&#x201C;EB-5 Investors&#x201D;) seeking lawful permanent resident status based on their investment in a U.S. commercial enterprise. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">On December 27, 2016, the Company borrowed </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;">$52,000</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;"> from the Limited Partnerships to fund two capital projects at its Mount Snow ski resort. </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">The development projects include i) the West Lake Water Project, which was completed during fiscal 2018 and included the construction of a new water storage reservoir for snowmaking, and ii) the Carinthia Ski Lodge Project, which, as of April 30, 2018, is in progress and includes the construction of a new skier service building. The amounts were borrowed through two loan agreements, which provided </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$30,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> for the West Lake Water Project and </font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">$22,000</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;"> for the Carinthia Ski Lodge project (together, the &#x201C;EB-5 Development Notes&#x201D;).</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:10pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Amounts outstanding under the EB-5 Development Notes accrue simple interest at a fixed rate of </font><font style="display: inline;">1.0%</font><font style="display: inline;"> per annum until the maturity date, which is </font><font style="display: inline;">December 27, 2021</font><font style="display: inline;">, subject to extension of up to an additional two years at the option of the borrowers with lender consent. If the maturity date is extended, amounts outstanding under the EB-5 Development Notes will accrue simple interest at a fixed rate of </font><font style="display: inline;">7.0%</font><font style="display: inline;"> per annum during the first year of extension and a fixed rate of </font><font style="display: inline;">10.0%</font><font style="display: inline;"> per annum during the second year of extension. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Upon an event of default (as defined), amounts outstanding under the EB-5 Development Notes shall bear interest at the rate of </font><font style="display: inline;">5.0%</font><font style="display: inline;"> per annum, subject to the extension increases. For so long as amounts under the EB-5 Development Notes are outstanding, the Company is restricted from taking certain actions without the consent of the lenders, including, but not limited to transferring or disposing of the properties or assets financed with the loan proceeds. In addition, the Company is prohibited from prepaying outstanding amounts owed if such prepayment would jeopardize any of the EB-5 Investors from being admitted to the U.S. via the EB-5 Program. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">has evaluated the </font><font style="display: inline;">facts and circumstances surrounding the Limited </font><font style="display: inline;">Partnership</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">a</font><font style="display: inline;">nd determined the </font><font style="display: inline;">Limited </font><font style="display: inline;">Partnership do not require consolidation in the Company&#x2019;s financial statements as the Company does not have a variable interest in the Limited Partnerships</font><font style="display: inline;"> under either the variable interest model or the voting interest model, </font><font style="display: inline;">as substantive participation rights give the limited partners the ability to effectively participate in significant decisions that would be expected to be made in the ordinary course of the </font><font style="display: inline;">L</font><font style="display: inline;">imited </font><font style="display: inline;">P</font><font style="display: inline;">artnerships</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;"> business and thereby preclude the Company as general partner from exercising unilateral control over the partnerships. </font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 8pt;line-height:105%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">On October 27, 2017, the Company renewed and increased its existing credit facility with Royal Banks of Missouri (the &#x201C;2017 Royal Banks Credit Facility&#x201D;). The 2017 Royal Banks Credit Facility provides for a </font><font style="display: inline;">$10,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> working capital line of credit to be used for general business purposes and a </font><font style="display: inline;">$15,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> acquisition line of credit to be used i) to pay off </font><font style="display: inline;">$12,415</font><font style="display: inline;"> of principal and accrued interest outstanding under the previous credit agreement with Royal Banks of Missouri (the &#x201C;Original Credit Facility&#x201D;) and ii) for the acquisition of additional ski resort properties. On October 27, 2017, the Company used the borrowing capacity available under the acquisition line of credit to pay off the amount outstanding under the Original Credit Facility, including amounts outstanding under term loan described in the table above as Royal Banks of Missouri Debt. </font><a name="_Hlk500161537"></a><font style="display: inline;">As of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">April 30, 2018</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">$12,415</font><font style="display: inline;"> was outstanding under the acquisition line of credit and nothing was outstanding under the working capital line of credit. </font><font style="display: inline;">$10,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">$2,585</font><font style="display: inline;"> was unused and available under the working capital line of credit and acquisition line of credit, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The term of the 2017 Royal Banks Credit Facility is </font><font style="display: inline;">14</font><font style="display: inline;"> months with loans payable in monthly interest only installments charged at the bank&#x2019;s prime rate plus </font><font style="display: inline;">1.00%</font><font style="display: inline;"> per annum, with any outstanding principal amounts due in </font><font style="display: inline;">December 2018</font><font style="display: inline;">. As of April 30, 2018, the Company had </font><font style="display: inline;">$508</font><font style="display: inline;"> in restricted cash to fund a debt service account for the estimated interest payments due through the end of calendar 2018 in connection with outstanding loans under the 2017 Royal Banks Credit Facility. The Company is required to maintain a minimum debt service coverage ratio (as defined in the credit agreement) of </font><font style="display: inline;">1.25</font><font style="display: inline;">:1.00. In addition, were the Company&#x2019;s fixed charge coverage ratio (as defined in the credit agreement) to fall below </font><font style="display: inline;">1.50</font><font style="display: inline;">:1.00, the Company would be required to prefund certain other debt service payments, and should the ratio fall below </font><font style="display: inline;">1.25</font><font style="display: inline;">:1.00, the Company would be prohibited from paying dividends. The 2017 Royal Banks Credit Facility is secured by the assets of the Company&#x2019;s subsidiaries which operate its Hidden Valley, Paoli Peaks, Snow Creek, Crotched Mountain and Attitash resorts.</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Stockholders&#x2019; Agreement</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">On November 2, 2016, in connection with the closing of the Private Placement, the Company entered into the Stockholders&#x2019; Agreement (the &#x201C;Stockholders&#x2019; Agreement&#x201D;) which, among other provisions, i) provides the Investor a right to nominate a director to sit on the Company&#x2019;s board of directors so long as the Investor beneficially owns, on a fully diluted, as-converted basis, at least </font><font style="display: inline;">20%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of the outstanding equity securities of the Company, ii) restricts transfers of the Company&#x2019;s securities by the Investor and certain management shareholders (the &#x201C;Management Stockholders&#x201D;), iii) provides the Investor with a right of first offer to purchase shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock from the </font><font style="display: inline;">M</font><font style="display: inline;">anagement Stockholders, iv) grants the Investor preemptive rights with respect to future issuances of securities, </font><font style="display: inline;">and </font><font style="display: inline;">v) requires the Investor</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s approval, so long as it meets certain ownership requirements (as defined), in order for the Company to a) materially change the nature of its business or b) acquire or dispose of any resorts, assets or properties for aggregate consideration equal to or greater than </font><font style="display: inline;">30%</font><font style="display: inline;"> of the enterprise value (as defined) of the Company and its subsidiaries. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">6.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 36pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Restructuring and Impairment</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During the year ended April 30, 2018, the Company incurred restructuring and impairment charges of </font><font style="display: inline;">$1,691</font><font style="display: inline;"> in connection with its decision to cease operation of a restaurant and certain hotel-like amenities at a condominium building adjacent to its Attitash ski resort (the &#x201C;Attitash Hotel Closure&#x201D;). In connection with the Company&#x2019;s 2007 acquisition of its Attitash ski resort, the Company acquired property and equipment constituting the commercial core of a condominium building located adjacent to the resort. Since this acquisition, the Company i) provided management services to the condominium&#x2019;s owners association under a management services agreement (the &#x201C;Management Services Agreement&#x201D;), ii) sponsored a rental management program whereby unoccupied condominium units were rented as hotel rooms, and iii) operated restaurant and other hotel-type amenities. In December 2017, the Company determined it would not be able to renew the Management Services Agreement upon its expiration on April 30, 2018 and, as a result, decided to terminate the rental management program and cease operation of the hotel-type amenities as of that date. The charges included </font><font style="display: inline;">$1,586</font><font style="display: inline;"> of asset impairment charges, </font><font style="display: inline;">$36</font><font style="display: inline;"> of severance expense and </font><font style="display: inline;">$70</font><font style="display: inline;"> of other costs. As of April 30, 2018, no amounts were accrued for costs associated with the Attitash Hotel Closure, and the Company expects it may incur future additional charges in the range of </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">The Company assesses available positive and negative evidence to estimate if sufficient future taxable income will be generated to use the existing deferred tax assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Significant pieces of objective negative evidence evaluated included i) the shorter net operating loss carryforward period associated with a certain state in which the Company operates and ii) the amounts of taxable income apportioned to that taxing jurisdiction over the three-year period ended April 30, 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such objective evidence limits the Company&#x2019;s ability to consider other subjective evidence, such as projections for future growth.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Based on its evaluation, the Company concluded it is more likely than not that the benefit of net operating loss carryforwards associated with that state will not be fully realized.&nbsp;&nbsp;In recognition of that risk the Company established a valuation allowance of $350 as of April 30, 2018, to reduce the carrying value of deferred tax assets related to those state net operating loss carryforwards.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount of the deferred tax assets considered realizable, however, could be adjusted in the future if estimates of future taxable income during the carryforward period are reduced or increased or if objective negative evidence is no longer present, thus allowing additional weight to be given to subjective evidence such as the Company&#x2019;s projections for growth. </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On December 22, 2017, the United States government enacted comprehensive tax legislation commonly referred to as the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (the &#x201C;2017 Tax Act&#x201D;). The 2017 Tax Act made broad changes to the federal tax code which impacts the Company. The 2017 Tax Act included provisions that, among other things, provides for i) the reduction of the federal corporate tax rate, ii) the elimination of the corporate alternative minimum tax, iii) a new limitation on the deductibility of interest expense, iv) changes in the treatment of net operating losses after December 31, 2017, and v) bonus depreciation that allows for full expensing of qualified property.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The 2018 change in federal statutory rate as appearing in the table above, consists of two components related to the 2017 Tax Act.&nbsp;&nbsp;First, the Company recognized a discrete benefit at the enactment date of the 2017 Tax Act of </font><font style="display: inline;">$124</font><font style="display: inline;"> based on remeasurement of net deferred tax liabilities at that date utilizing the reduced corporate </font><font style="display: inline;">tax </font><font style="display: inline;">rate of </font><font style="display: inline;">21%</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">implemented by t</font><font style="display: inline;">he 2017 Tax Act.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">In addition, the reconciliation from the federal tax rate above applies a blended rate based on a </font><font style="display: inline;">34%</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">corporate tax </font><font style="display: inline;">rate for the first eight months of </font><font style="display: inline;">fiscal 2018 </font><font style="display: inline;">and a </font><font style="display: inline;">21%</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">corporate tax </font><font style="display: inline;">rate for the last four months of </font><font style="display: inline;">fiscal 2018</font><font style="display: inline;">. However, as the Company is a calendar year taxpayer and its business is seasonal, cumulative losses result during the first eight months of the fiscal year that are partially offset by income in the four month period ending April 30, 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;Consequently, the actual tax rates applicable to the Company&#x2019;s full year pretax loss are substantially </font><font style="display: inline;">different t</font><font style="display: inline;">han the blended rate, resulting in an additional beneficial impact of approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$3,487</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company accounts for unrecognized tax benefits also in accordance with ASC 740, which prescribes a minimum probability threshold that a tax position must meet before a financial statement benefit is recognized. The minimum threshold is defined as a tax position that is more likely than not to be sustained upon examination by the applicable taxing authority, including resolution to any related appeals or litigation, based solely on the technical merits of the position. </font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In November 2005, </font><font style="display: inline;">the Company sold its Mad River Mountain ski resort and simultaneously leased the property back for a period of 21 years</font><font style="display: inline;">. The resulting gain on the sale was deferred and is being ratably recognized in income over the term of the lease.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">11.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 36pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Employee Benefit Plan</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company maintains a tax-deferred savings plan for all eligible employees. Employees become eligible to participate after attaining the age of </font><font style="display: inline;">21</font><font style="display: inline;"> and completing </font><font style="display: inline;">one</font><font style="display: inline;"> year of service. Employee contributions to the plan are tax-deferred under Section 401(k) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. Company matching contributions are made at the discretion of the board of directors. </font><font style="display: inline;">No</font><font style="display: inline;"> contributions were made in fiscal years 2018, 2017, and 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">12.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 36pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">Concentrations of Credit Risk and Fair Value Measures</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Concentrations of Credit Risk</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s financial instruments that are exposed to concentrations of credit risk consist primarily of cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash. The Company&#x2019;s cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash are on deposit with financial institutions where such balances will, at times, be in excess of federally insured limits. The Company has not experienced any losses associated with such deposits.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Fair Value of Measurements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company measures the fair value of assets and liabilities using a three-tier fair value hierarchy which prioritizes the inputs used in measuring fair value as follows: Level&nbsp;1&nbsp;- observable inputs such as quoted prices in active markets; Level&nbsp;2&nbsp;- inputs, other than quoted market prices in active markets, which are observable, either directly or indirectly; and Level&nbsp;3&nbsp;- valuations derived from valuation techniques in which one or more significant inputs are unobservable.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the Company may use various valuation techniques, including the market approach, using comparable market prices; the income approach, using present value of future income or cash flow; and the cost approach, using the replacement cost of assets. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">The Company </font><font style="display: inline;">estimated</font><font style="display: inline;"> the fair value of the EPR Secured Notes, EB-5 Development </font><font style="display: inline;">N</font><font style="display: inline;">o</font><font style="display: inline;">tes</font><font style="display: inline;"> and Wildcat Mountain Note using </font><font style="display: inline;">a discounted cash flow approach and </font><font style="display: inline;">Level 2 inputs</font><font style="display: inline;">, including</font><font style="display: inline;"> market borrowing yields for instruments of similar maturities. The Company estimated the fair value of the Series A Preferred Stock </font><font style="display: inline;">and related warrants and other features </font><font style="display: inline;">using Level 2 inputs</font><font style="display: inline;">, including market yields for similar instruments</font><font style="display: inline;">. The Company estimated the fair value of capital leases and other borrowings to approximate their carrying value. </font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company is periodically involved in various claims and legal proceedings, many of which occur in the normal course of business. Management routinely assesses the likelihood of adverse judgments or outcomes, including consideration of its insurance coverage and, i</font><font style="display: inline;">n the opinion of the Company&#x2019;s management, the ultimate liabilities resulting from such claims and proceedings will not have a material adverse effect on its business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Leases</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company leases certain land, land improvements, buildings and equipment under noncancelable operating leases. Certain of the leases contain escalation provisions based generally on changes in the consumer price index with maximum annual percentage increases capped at rates between </font><font style="display: inline;">1.5%</font><font style="display: inline;"> to </font><font style="display: inline;">4.5%</font><font style="display: inline;">. Additionally, certain leases contain contingent rental provisions which are based on revenue. The Company paid no significant contingent rentals in the periods presented.</font><font style="display: inline;"> Rent expense under operating leases for the years ended April 30, 2018, 2017 and 2016, was </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">2,</font><font style="display: inline;">548</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">$1,669</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">$1,732</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The provisions of certain of the Company&#x2019;s debt instruments require that the Company make and maintain deposits</font><font style="display: inline;"> with third party financial instit</font><font style="display: inline;">ut</font><font style="display: inline;">ions</font><font style="display: inline;">, to be held in escrow for the benefit of the lender, in an amount equal to the estimated minimum interest payment for the upcoming fiscal year.&nbsp;&nbsp;When funded, these amounts are included in restricted cash on the consolidated balance sheets.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 10.8pt 0pt 0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company&#x2019;s management, with the participation of the Company&#x2019;s Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, evaluated the effectiveness of the Company&#x2019;s disclosure controls and procedures (as that term is defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">(</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">the &#x201C;Exchange Act&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">)</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, as of the end of the period covered by this </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Report</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. Based on that evaluation, management, with the participation of the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, concluded that the Company&#x2019;s disclosure controls and procedures, as of the end of the period covered by this </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Report</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, are functioning effectively to provide reasonable assurance that the information required to be disclosed by the Company in reports filed under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the rules and forms</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> of the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">SEC </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">and is accumulated and communicated to the Company&#x2019;s management, including its Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> A controls system, no matter how well designed and operated, cannot provide absolute assurance that the objectives of the controls system are met, and no evaluation of controls can provide absolute assurance that all control issues and instances of fraud, if any, within a company have been detected.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 10.8pt 0pt 0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

Management has assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">April</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;30, 201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">8</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;based on criteria established in Internal Control-Integrated Framework (2013) issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission. As a result of this assessment, management concluded that, as of April&nbsp;30, 201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">8</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, our internal control over financial reporting was effective</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">This </font><font style="display: inline;">Report</font><font style="display: inline;"> does not include an attestation report of our independent registered public accounting firm</font><font style="display: inline;"> pursuant to</font><font style="display: inline;"> the rules of the </font><font style="display: inline;">SEC</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">for </font><font style="display: inline;">emerging growth</font><font style="display: inline;"> companies.</font>
